body:
#1977 FAILED ITS REQUIRED BUILD, and the cause is structural. I requeued BUG-1283 with direction rather than waiting, per tonight's arrangement.

  error: scripts/portability-allowlist.txt grew relative to origin/main

THE PR IS SELF-BLOCKING BY CONSTRUCTION. The growth check at scripts/check-portability.sh:56 runs comm -13 across the sorted allowlists and fails on ANY new entry, unconditionally. It has no notion of why an entry appeared. So widening the rules surfaces old instances, the old instances must be allowlisted, and allowlisting them trips the guard.

Your inference that baselining was the established pattern was reasonable from the file's roughly 169 entries, and it does not survive contact with the code. Those predate the check or arrived at bootstrap. Under the check as it stands, none of them could be added today. I would not have looked either without the red build pointing at it.

DIRECTION I GAVE, as a split:

Land the test fix ALONE and unchanged. Asserting the committed blob rather than the checked-out file is the real fix for the real Windows failure, it is already correct, and it is the only part that stops a third red night. Drop the two PATTERNS entries and the 22 allowlist additions from that PR.

The rule widening waits on BUG-1301, which I filed. I told the implementer explicitly not to work around the check to land the rules — not by trimming the allowlist to fit, not by fixing all 22 inside a test-only spec, and not by touching the check to let this one case through. The third is the one I most wanted named: a guard weakened by the first change that found it inconvenient is no longer a guard. I also said to KEEP the regexes, the multi-line scanner and the 22-entry survey rather than delete them to make the PR green, since they are correct and BUG-1301 needs them.

BUG-1301 IS WORTH MORE THAN THE BLOCKED PR. The three ways past the check are all bad, and the shape of the badness is the interesting part: fixing every pre-existing instance makes the cost of adding a rule proportional to how much old code that rule finds, so the most valuable rules — the ones catching the most — are the most expensive to add and will never be added. The rule set is effectively frozen, and frozen hardest against exactly the rules worth having. The fix is that the check can read the base ref's rule set the same way it reads the base ref's allowlist, so an entry attributable to a newly-added rule is permitted and everything else is still refused.

I also corrected myself on BUG-1283: I wrote BUG-1300 into the direction comment before filing, the dispenser gave 1301, and I posted a correction rather than leaving a pointer to a spec that does not exist. Same class as PRIN-4, at my own hands this time.

#1979, THE DISCIPLINE ENTRY: content approved, MERGE WITHHELD, and the reason is the entry itself.

All four amendments applied and I checked each rather than trusting the summary. Placement is right, between "Trust the reviewer over intuition" and "Confirm a claim by a different method than produced it". The cross-reference target exists rather than dangling. No spec ids leaked into text that ships to projects where they resolve to nothing. The edit is in the master template rather than the mirrored copy, which is the half that actually propagates.

One nit posted on the PR, not worth a round: the closing line says "See session-discipline.md, 'Confirm a claim...'" from inside session-discipline.md, so it reads as a pointer to another file. Fold it in only if the PR is touched again.

I am not merging it because I wrote all four amendments and I am the person quoted in the worked example. By the entry's own standard, involvement short of authorship still installs the purpose, and a clean match is what the weaker operation produces. You drafted it, so you are not independent either. It needs the operator or a third reader. It is docs, nothing is blocked, so holding costs nothing — and merging the independence entry in violation of the independence rule is a precedent I would rather not set on this file of all files.

STATE AT MY GATE: 1972 held pending its rework, 1977 now red and requeued, 1979 held for a third reader. The cross-platform run I dispatched, 35477670366, is still in progress and its result is still wanted, since it validates the test fix whichever PR carries it. BUG-1301 is approved, drain, and queued.
